land.text: Wagadu and Koumbi Saleh: 'By 1203, the Sosso had risen against their masters and conquered Ghana. Diara Kante took control of Koumbi Saleh'

successors.note: Sosso page infobox dates the capture of Wagadu to c. 1200, the Ghana page says 'by 1203'; Cliopatria hands the same 204,203 km2 shape from Ghana (to 1201) to Sosso (from 1202), and the dossier follows Cliopatria's years. The Ghana kings carried on as vassals of Soumaoro (Soumaba Cisse, 1203-1235) and then as allies of Mali, so the Ghana line did not vanish.

capitals.name: Koumbi Saleh (Kumbi Saleh)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Koumbi Saleh (likely a later capital)'. Al-Bakri (1067/68) described two cities 10 km apart; al-Idrisi (1154) a later royal city on a river that may not be Koumbi Saleh; Dierk Lange puts the core near Lake Faguibine. Coordinates are the gazetteer's historic-site point; the page gives none.

keyframe_review.note: 204,203 km2 (bbox 8.6-3.8 W, 13.3-17.6 N, south-east Mauritania and western Mali) against the infobox's 650,000 km2 'Area (1000)': ratio 0.31, outside the factor of two. The infobox figure rests on the page's oral-tradition list of lands 'under its control at its height' (Takrur, Jafunu, Jaara, Bakhunu, Neema, Soso, Guidimakha, Guidime, Gajaaga, Awker, Adrar, Hodh), which the page does not date and the Takrur page does not support as vassalage; the shape is therefore taken as the directly ruled core around Koumbi Saleh and the infobox figure as a tribute sphere. Awdaghust (990-1053) lies outside the shape and is added by the next entry. The page gives 'Dyabe Cisse: 790s' in its king list, matching the shape's 793 start; its 'Established c. 300' is not mapped (no territory described).

union.text: Awdaghust, conquered by Ghana in 990 and held under a Ghanaian governor until it fell to the Almoravids in 1054

correction.text: The Ghana core with Awdaghust and its district added, 990-1053

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 990-1053: the core plus Awdaghust. the page dates Ghana's conquest of Awdaghust 'In 990', after which it installed its own governor, and says Awdaghust 'fell to the Almoravids in 1054'. Awdaghust (10.4 W, 17.4 N) is west of the Cliopatria bbox (8.6 W).

Same cells and area as the 793 shape. The page's 'conquered by the Almoravid dynasty in 1076-77' is a historiographical tradition that Conrad and Fisher call 'merely perpetuated folklore'; Lange also rejects a conquest; the page says only that the country 'certainly did convert to Islam around 1076'. No territorial change is dated at 1085, so the shape stands unchanged from the 793 one.

Same shape again. Nothing on the page dates a change at 1192 (the king list gives Diara Kante 1180-1202). The shape runs to 1201; the Sosso capture is c. 1200 (Sosso page) or 'by 1203' (Ghana page), so the end year is within the pages' own spread.

region.text: southeast Mauritania and western Mali, around Koumbi Saleh

ledger.note: 793: Wagadu, the Ghana empire of the Soninke, appears in the Sahel around Koumbi Saleh. The page's king list gives 'Dyabe Cisse: 790s' and oral tradition has Dyabe 'founding Wagadu' after a succession dispute; the infobox gives 'Established: c. 300' and the page puts the rise of Wagadu from the Tichitt culture at the end of the 3rd century, with no territory described, so the map starts at Cliopatria's 793.

region.text: Awdaghust, west of the Wagadu core

ledger.note: 990: Ghana conquers Awdaghust and installs its own governor. The page dates the conquest 'In 990' and says Ghana then installed its own governor. It names no ruler or people of Awdaghust.
1054: Awdaghust falls to the Almoravids. Awdaghust 'fell to the Almoravids in 1054' (Cliopatria's Almoravid shapes begin only in 1056).

1201: the Sosso take Wagadu. 'By 1203, the Sosso had risen against their masters and conquered Ghana. Diara Kante took control of Koumbi Saleh'; the Sosso page's infobox says 'Capture of Wagadu: c. 1200'. The year is bridged to Cliopatria's hand-over (Ghana to 1201, Sosso from 1202); the pages' own spread is c. 1200 to 1203.

region.text: the last Cliopatria shape of the empire

ledger.note: 1201: Ghana ends as an independent empire. The Ghana kings continue as vassals of Soumaoro Kante (Soumaba Cisse, 1203-1235) and later as allies of Mali, 'the Ghana's role as an ally declined to that of a submissive state' (Mali's rise); 'Koumbi Saleh was abandoned sometime in the 15th century'. The infobox gives two end dates, 'c. 15th century' and 'c. mid-13th century'.

wars.name: Ghana's conquest of Awdaghust
wars.outcome: Ghana took Awdaghust and installed its own governor.
wars.note: The page names no opponent and gives only the year.

wars.name: Almoravid capture of Awdaghust
wars.outcome: Awdaghust passed from Ghana to the Almoravids.

wars.name: Ghana and Sila
wars.outcome: No territorial result is given. 'Sila was at war with Ghana in the 1060s'; in 1083 Ghana asked Almoravid help against Tadmekka and Silla.
wars.note: The Takrur page instead puts a war between Silla, 'a vassal of Takrur', and Wagadu in the 12th century; the two pages disagree on the century.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Ghana (disputed)
wars.outcome: Disputed: a tradition has the Almoravids conquering Ghana in 1076-77; Conrad and Fisher call this folklore and Lange agrees there was no conquest; Ghana converted to Islam around 1076. No border change is recorded.
wars.note: Kept in the list so the reviewer sees it was considered; no ledger event is written for it.

wars.name: Sosso conquest of Ghana
wars.outcome: The Sosso took Koumbi Saleh and Wagadu; Diara Kante founded the Diarisso dynasty there and his son Soumaoro Kante exacted tribute.
wars.note: Sosso infobox 'Capture of Wagadu: c. 1200'; Barth dated it c. 1203 (Sosso page); Ghana page 'By 1203'.

certainty.note: Wagadu's frontiers are not described by any page opened: the Sahel and the tribute sphere are approximate. Awdaghust (990-1054) is a point on a trade route, not a bordered district.

sources.title: Ghana Empire
sources.note: Identity, king list, infobox area (650,000 km2 at 1000), Awdaghust 990/1054, the Almoravid dispute, the Sosso conquest 'by 1203', end.

sources.title: Sosso Empire
sources.note: Infobox 'Capture of Wagadu: c. 1200', Barth's c. 1203; Soumaoro and Diara Kante.

notes: Cliopatria's three Ghana shapes (793-1084, 1085-1191, 1192-1201) are identical (204,203 km2); the same cells are the Sosso shapes of 1202-1235. Open points: (1) the page's founding c. 300 and the tribute sphere of 650,000 km2 are not mapped (no dated territory); the oral-tradition vassals (Takrur, Jafunu, Jaara, Bakhunu, Neema, Soso, Guidimakha, Guidime, Gajaaga, Awker, Adrar, Hodh) are not written as vassal events because the page dates none and the Takrur page says Lebi allied with the Almoravids 'to counter the power of the Ghana Empire' rather than describing vassalage. A gap-filler could open the works the page cites (al-Bakri, Conrad and Fisher, Lange). (2) The Almoravid 'conquest' of 1076-77 is recorded as a disputed war only. (3) The Ghana-Sila war is dated to the 1060s by the Ghana page and to the 12th century by the Takrur page. (4) Ghana's end year: c. 1200 (Sosso page), 'by 1203' (Ghana and Mali pages, Barth), 1201 (Cliopatria, kept). (5) The Ghana kings continued as vassals of Sosso (Soumaba Cisse 1203-1235) and as allies then submissive to Mali; not drawn.
